principles: Fail closed for lifecycle gates that affect phase advancement.
Keep one typed registry as the visible source for lifecycle facts before large refactors.
Preserve user-maintained guidance while syncing managed assets.
Make every behavior change observable through a focused smoke or contract test.
drivers: Reduce risk of silent phase advancement with missing validation evidence.
Lower future lifecycle maintenance drift across phase graph, machine, command policy, and renderer hints.
Deliver V0/V1 without destabilizing the broader story_advance flow.

options.name: A: V0 fail-closed plus read-only lifecycle registry foundation
pros: Closes the highest-risk fail-open behavior first.
Creates a single visible registry without forcing a risky full migration immediately.
Keeps external CLI behavior compatible except for formerly unsafe exceptions.
cons: Some duplicate lifecycle sources remain until later V2 migration.
Registry initially detects drift rather than fully generating all consumers.

options.name: B: Full lifecycle registry migration and story_advance decomposition now
pros: Could make transition, gate, effects, and renderer all registry-driven in one story.
cons: Much larger blast radius across phase advancement, DONE merge, hooks, and reviewer gates.
Harder to distinguish regressions from intended behavior changes.
Managed asset drift and validate fail-open would remain open longer while refactor is underway.

options.name: C: Only patch validate and managed assets, defer registry
cons: Does not address the root single-truth-source problem.
Future phase changes would still have no registry contract to catch drift.

chosen: A: V0 fail-closed plus read-only lifecycle registry foundation
rationale: Option A fixes the current safety issues while creating a typed registry foothold and contract coverage. It keeps this high-risk framework story bounded and sets up the larger V2 decomposition without combining every risky migration into one change.

preMortem.scenario: Fail-closed change blocks valid TEST advancement due to no-validator warn path
preMortem.trigger: A project has no validate.ts and no configured command, but workflow policy still expects validation semantics.
preMortem.consequence: Express or light stories become unusable because skipped validation is treated as infrastructure failure rather than policy-controlled warning.
preMortem.mitigation: Only convert verifier execution/import/parse exceptions to hard failures; preserve structured validate JSON with allPass/status semantics for policy-controlled warn/fail decisions.

preMortem.scenario: Managed asset sync erases local AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md guidance
preMortem.trigger: Using koala check --apply on STALE_LOCAL_EDIT managed sections without manual preservation.
preMortem.consequence: Repository-specific workflow rules are lost and future agents follow incomplete guidance.
preMortem.mitigation: Handle CASE_MISMATCH manually and keep local docs intact; only adjust managed markers/templates when local content is preserved or moved explicitly.

preMortem.scenario: Registry becomes a new duplicate source instead of reducing drift
preMortem.trigger: Adding lifecycle-registry.ts but leaving phase-flow/context/tests unconstrained.
preMortem.consequence: Maintainers now have one more lifecycle table to update with no mechanical benefit.
preMortem.mitigation: Add contract/smoke assertions comparing registry transitions, event mapping, legacy aliases, and command policy expectations in the same story.
